content: === Introduction ===
Dysmelia (from the Greek dys (δυσ-), "bad" + mélos (μέλος), "limb" + English suffix -ia) is a congenital disorder of a limb resulting from a disturbance in embryonic development.[1]
=== Types ===
Dysmelia can refer to [citation needed]
<info> missing (aplasia) limbs: amelia (including tetraamelia), oligodactyly, congenital amputation e.g. tibial or radial aplasia
<info> malformation of limbs: shortening (micromelia, rhizomelia or mesomelia), ectrodactyly, phocomelia, meromelia, syndactyly, brachydactyly, club foot
<info> extra limbs: polymelia, polydactyly, polysyndactyly
=== Occurrence rate ===
Birth defects involving limbs occur in 0.69 per 1000.[2]
=== Causes ===
Dysmelia can be caused by[citation needed]
<info> Inheritance of abnormal genes, e.g. polydactyly, ectrodactyly or brachydactyly, symptoms of deformed limbs then often occur in combination with other symptoms (syndromes)
<info> external causes during pregnancy (thus not inherited), e.g. via amniotic band syndrome
<info> teratogenic drugs (e.g. thalidomide, which causes phocomelia) or environmental chemicals
<info> ionizing radiation (nuclear weapons, radioiodine, radiation therapy)
=== Syndromes with dysmelia ===
<info> Autosomal recessive Robinow syndrome
<info> Basel–Vanagaite–Sirota syndrome (Microlissencephaly-Micromelia syndrome)
<info> Fibular dimelia diplopodia syndrome (Leg duplication mirror foot syndrome)
<info> Mesomelia-Synostoses syndrome (8q13 microdeletion syndrome)
<info> Roberts SC-Phocomelia syndrome (Phocomelia syndrome)
<info> Split-hand split-foot malformation (SHFM)
<info> TAR syndrome (thrombocytopenia with absent radius)
